decision.title: Security review — adversarial (attacker) pass — retroactive review of DDR-179 permission gate (commit `4174b82e`)
decision.rationale: **Date:** 2026-07-16 · **Reviewer:** `ethical-hacker` (flow plugin) · **Scope:** already-committed permission-gate code, never previously reviewed despite the plan's own Validation §7 requiring it 4 blockers, composed into 1 High/Critical exploit chain. **All four fixed before commit** — see DDR-179's addendum for the full writeup and resolution details. `PermissionPrompt.jsx`'s `firstAllow = options.find(o => o.kind === 'allow_once' || o.kind === 'allow_always')` returns whichever kind the ADAPTER lists first. The real adapter's own option ordering for a standard tool-call request is `[allow_always, allow_once, reject_once]` — `allow_always` at index `[0]`. A user pressing Enter or clicking the one visually-dominant (`btn--primary`-styled `allow_always`) button believed they were approving one action; they were actually granting a session-scoped standing exemption. This defeats DDR-179's entire stated purpose using nothing but the shipped UI's own default affordances.
